title: Quantifying Risk Propensities of Large Language Models: Ethical Focus and Bias Detection through Role-Play

bias_targets.methodology: Prompting LLMs to role-play as specific professions (e.g., doctor, artist, teacher, politician, farmer) and measuring their perceived risk propensities and ethical attitudes using the DOSPERT and EDRAS scales.

Simulating personas with varying levels of education (e.g., secondary technical school, bachelor, doctorate) and institutional tiers (e.g., junior college, top 10 universities) to evaluate their ethical risk scores via the EDRAS scale.

Configuring LLMs to role-play as individuals from different racial and ethnic backgrounds (e.g., African American, Chinese Han, White American) and assessing differences in risk propensities using the DOSPERT scale.
Comparing the simulated risk-taking behaviors and propensities (e.g., likelihood of buying illegal drugs, cheating on exams) of male versus female personas using psychological risk scales.
